aiSettingsDialog.description: You can temporarily adjust the trading style and risk tolerance for this action:

trends.title: Trends & Moving Averages
trends.what: The average price of gold over recent periods (like the last 20 or 50 candles). It is like looking at a student's average GPA to understand their overall performance.
trends.when: To identify the overall market direction. If the price is above the average, it is an uptrend (buy); if below, it is a downtrend (sell).
trends.example: If the gold price is $2350 and the 20-period average is $2300, the market has bullish momentum and buying is preferred.

rsi.title: Relative Strength Index (RSI)
rsi.what: Measures the speed and strength of price movements, ranging from 0 to 100. It is like a car speedometer indicating how fast we are accelerating.
rsi.when: Above 70 (Overbought): The market is too hot and a price drop is likely (sell). Below 30 (Oversold): The market is too cheap and buyers are ready to enter (buy). Between 30 and 70: Normal conditions.
rsi.example: When RSI hits 80, buyers are exhausted and the price will likely drop soon. Avoid buying at this point.

atr.title: Volatility Indicator (ATR)
atr.what: Shows how much the gold price fluctuates up and down in a given timeframe (market turbulence). It is like the height of sea waves—stormy or calm.
atr.when: To set stop loss and take profit levels. In a stormy market (high ATR), place the stop loss further away to avoid being stopped out by minor swings. In a calm market (low ATR), keep it closer.
atr.example: If the 5m ATR is $2, gold fluctuates about $2 every 5 minutes. Do not set a stop loss of only $0.50, as it will be triggered quickly.

levels.title: Support & Resistance Levels
levels.what: Support (Floor): A price level where buyers step in and prevent the price from falling lower. Resistance (Ceiling): A price level where sellers prevent the price from rising higher.
levels.when: Buy near support (floor) and sell near resistance (ceiling). Breaking these levels indicates the start of a strong new movement.
levels.example: If gold repeatedly bounces up from $2300, $2300 is strong support. Buying near $2300 is a good opportunity.

ob.title: Order Blocks (OB)
ob.what: Price zones where major banks and financial institutions placed heavy buy or sell orders, leaving behind a trace of large orders.
ob.when: When price returns to this zone, unfilled orders are activated, causing a strong price reversal. We trade along with them in these areas.
ob.example: A buy order block forms at $2310. When the price returns to $2310 later, we buy along with the institutional order flow.

fvg.title: Fair Value Gaps (FVG)
fvg.what: When the price surges or drops extremely fast, it leaves an empty space (gap) in the chart. The market acts like a magnet, wanting to return and fill this empty space.
fvg.when: To predict temporary price retracements. The price usually returns to fill the gap before continuing its path. We wait for it to return to this zone to enter.
fvg.example: Gold surges from $2320 to $2340, leaving a gap. We wait for the price to drop back to $2325 (filling the gap) and buy.

structure.title: Market Structure Breaks (BOS/CHoCH)
structure.what: Indicates a change in market direction or the continuation of a strong trend. CHoCH (Change of Character) is the first sign of a reversal, and BOS (Break of Structure) confirms the trend is continuing.
structure.when: To join new trends. CHoCH tells us the trend has reversed. BOS tells us the trend is continuing, so we can hold or add to our positions.
structure.example: Gold has been falling. Suddenly, it breaks above the previous high (forming a CHoCH). This means the downtrend is over, and it's time to buy.
